title: FAMU vs Morehouse: control, tuition, size
summary: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) versus Morehouse College (Morehouse). Also searched as Morehouse vs FAMU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University vs Morehouse College (FAMU vs Morehouse) differ primarily in ownership, size, cost, and location. FAMU is a public institution located in Tallahassee with an undergraduate enrollment of 7,582 students. In contrast, Morehouse College is a private nonprofit college situated in Atlanta, enrolling 2,844 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary significantly, with FAMU charging $5,785 for in-state students, whereas Morehouse's in-state tuition is $32,893. These distinctions highlight differences in institutional structure, scale, and financial investment for students.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University vs Morehouse College (FAMU vs Morehouse). FAMU, as a public university, offers a substantially lower in-state tuition of $5,785 compared to Morehouse College's private tuition of $32,893. For out-of-state students, FAMU charges $17,725, while Morehouse maintains the same tuition rate of $32,893 regardless of residency. Regarding student debt, the median debt for FAMU graduates who complete their programs is $23,548, slightly less than Morehouse graduates, whose median debt stands at $25,000. These figures reflect the financial commitments students can expect at each institution.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University vs Morehouse College (FAMU vs Morehouse) differ in their learning environments and campus settings. FAMU, located in Tallahassee, Florida, serves a larger undergraduate population of 7,582 students, reflecting its status as a public university. Morehouse College, a private institution in Atlanta, Georgia, enrolls 2,844 undergraduates, offering a more intimate campus experience. These differences in size and location contribute to distinct academic and social atmospheres at each institution.

sections.heading: Pick FAMU if
paragraphs: Pick Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University vs Morehouse College (FAMU vs Morehouse) if you prefer a public institution with a lower admission rate of about 20.56%. FAMU offers a more affordable in-state tuition of $5,785, making it a cost-effective choice for Florida residents. Additionally, FAMU has a completion rate within 150% of normal time of approximately 53.35%, reflecting the proportion of students who finish their programs in a timely manner. These factors make FAMU a suitable option for students seeking accessible public education with reasonable graduation outcomes.

sections.heading: Pick Morehouse if
paragraphs: Pick Morehouse College if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with an admission rate of approximately 43.96%. Morehouse's tuition is significantly higher at $32,893, reflecting its private status and resources. The college also has a completion rate within 150% of normal time of about 59.44%, indicating a relatively strong student success rate. These factors make Morehouse a fitting choice for students seeking a private college experience with a moderate admission selectivity and a solid graduation outcome.
